newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker amid U.S. rate hike fears.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker amid U.S. rate hike fears.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on light volumes on Monday, climbing off earlier lows, as speculation that U.S. interest rates could rise next week weighed on both Canadian and U.S. markets, analysts said.
"The market is definitely getting ready for a Fed tightening here. They are putting every fear onto the plate," said one Toronto-based bond trader.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond dipped C$0.25 to C$109.27 to yield 7.206 percent against the U.S. 30-year benchmark, which fell 5/32 to yield 6.96 percent.

The spread between the two widened to 25 basis points from 24 basis points at the close of trading on Friday. The Canadian 30-year benchmark traded as low as C$108.82 in early afternoon trading, its lowest price since January.

"I would say it's all technical trading today. The bond market bounced back in the U.S. once it tested seven percent," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn Capital Inc.
Canadian bonds were pulled lower by U.S. treasuries, which fell to their lowest levels in almost six months amid concern U.S. rates could rise next week, analysts said.
Fueling speculation of a rate hike was a strong U.S. housing report and a hawkish speech in Germany by San Francisco Fed president Robert Parry.

Analysts said bond investors are now looking ahead to key Canadian and U.S. consumer price index data out this week. Canadian bond investors will also be watching testimony tomorrow by Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen before a Senate committee at 1000 EST/1500 GMT.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.21 to C$103.13 yielding 6.557 percent while the U.S. 10-year fell 5/32 to yield 6.72 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds was 16 basis points, unchanged from the close of trading on Friday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.03 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.26 percent.
